Ordinary Council Meeting - 30 September 2026

Wednesday, September 30, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 30 September 2026 at 5:30pm.

Summary of Decision(s):

Motion No. Item No Subject Motion
C.5634 8.1.1 Petition - Heritage Mute Swans That Council:
1. RECEIVES the petition submitted in relation to a request of establishing in-situ care and local protection for Northam’s 125-year heritage Mute Swans (Attachment 8.1.1.1); and
2. REFERS the petition to the Chief Executive Officer for consideration in accordance with clause 6.10 of the Shire of Northam Standing Orders Amendment Local Law 2018.
C.5635 9 APPLICATIONS FOR LEAVE OF ABSENCE That Council GRANTS Cr J E G Williams leave of absence from 13 November 2026 to 23 November 2026 (inclusive).
C.5636 10.1 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE ORDINARY COUNCIL MEETING HELD 18 AUGUST 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 18 August 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5637 10.2 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING HELD 3 SEPTEMBER 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Thursday, 3 September 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5638 10.3 NOTES FROM THE COUNCIL FORUM MEETING HELD 23 SEPTEMBER 2026 That Council RECEIVES the notes from the Council Forum meeting held on Wednesday, 23 September 2026.
C.5639 13.1.1 Council Policy Reviews That Council ADOPTS the following revised policies:
1. CP.18 Work Health Safety as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.2;
2. CP.32 Community Grants Program as provided in Attachment 13.1.14;
3. CP.35 Recognition of High Achievers as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.6;
4. CP.70 Donations Sponsorship Allocations as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.8;
5. CP.40 Asset Management Policy as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.10;
6. CP.61 Privacy as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.12 to REPLACE CP.61 Privacy, Information Handling and Breach of Information Policy as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.11;
7. CP.63 Information Breach Policy as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.13; and
8. CP.71 Independent Committee Members as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.18
C.5640 13.1.1 Council Policy Reviews That Council, by ABSOLUTE MAJORITY, in accordance with s.6.16 of the Local Government Act 1995:
1. ADOPTS the revised CP. 58 Property Management (Leases Licences) as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.15;
2. APPROVES the amended standard rate of $6.50 per square metre for recreational hangar sites;
3. APPROVES the amended standard rate of $6.75 per square metre for commercial hangar sites; and
4. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to give local public notice of the amended fees and charges in accordance with s. 6.19 of the Local Government Act 1995 and r. 3A of the Local Government (Administration) Regulations 1996.
C.5641 13.1.2 Lease of a portion of Lot 29079 on Reserve 44700 That Council:
1. ENDORSES, for the purpose of giving local public notice under section 3.58(3) of the Local Government Act 1995, the proposed lease of the whole of Lot 29079 (portion of Reserve 44700) to Mr Justin Fox, owner of 90 Fox Road, Burlong, for land management, vegetation management, bushfire fuel-load reduction and relocation of the boundary fence as shown in Figures 1 and 2 in Attachment 13.1.2.2.
2. ENDORSES the following proposed lease terms:
a. an initial term of ten (10) years, with one option to renew for a further ten (10) years;
b. a peppercorn rental, recognising the land management, fencing, maintenance and bushfire fuel-load management obligations to be undertaken by the lessee; and
c. grazing on Lot 29079 being prohibited until a suitable arrangement has been made with the owner of the adjoining property to the east to upgrade the eastern boundary fence to a standard suitable for containing livestock.
3. APPROVES the waiver of lease preparation, valuation and administration costs in accordance with Council Policy CP.58 Property Management (Leases and Licences).
4. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to give local public notice of the proposed disposition in accordance with sections 3.58(3) and (4) of the Local Government Act 1995, identifying the proposed peppercorn consideration and the assessed market rental of $1,000 per annum (refer Attachment 13.1.2.5).
5. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer, if no submissions are received during the public notice period, to finalise and execute the lease on the terms described in this resolution, subject to confirmation that the lease is permitted by the management order for Reserve 44700 and receipt of all approvals required under the Land Administration Act 1997, including section 18 approval.
6. REQUIRES the proposed lease to be brought back to Council for consideration before any agreement is entered into if submissions are received during the public notice period.
C.5642 13.2.1 Cemetery Maintenance Services That Council:
1. ENDORSES a transition to an in-house service delivery model for Cemetery maintenance services, involving one FTE position.
2. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to implement the transition, including confirmation of workload capacity, recruitment, asset requirements and operational arrangements.
3. NOTES that the 2026/27 budget includes one additional FTE within the Engineering Services department in accordance with the Shire’s Workforce Strategy 2025 to 2029.
4. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to report back to Council within 12 months of implementation on the performance and cost effectiveness of the in-house cemetery maintenance service delivery model, including actual costs, service performance, and workforce capacity.
C.5643 13.3.1 Lot 22 Gaden Road, Wundowie That Council:

1. REFUSES to approve the resubmitted Proposed Building Envelope Variation Plan dated 17 June 2026 as presented in Attachment 13.3.2.3.
2. ADVISES the applicant that:
a. The proposal to vary the existing building envelope, as shown on an approved Subdivision Guide Plan, is inconsistent with the objectives of the ‘Rural Residential Zone’ and is contrary to the intent of clause 4.31.7 of the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6; and
b. The proposed building envelope is not consistent with orderly and proper planning having due regard to the following considerations:
i. it would result in unnecessary and avoidable clearing of existing remnant native vegetation on the subject Lot 22 Gaden Road Wundowie;
ii. it would likely cause increased potential bushfire risk to future occupants of any new dwelling without further clearing;
iii. it would be detrimental to the established rural character, amenity and landscape and/or environmental qualities of the land and other properties in the locality; and
iv. it would set an expectation/precedent that the moving of a prescribed building envelopes into existing vegetated and/or high-risk areas can be done in undue circumstances.
C.5644 13.3.2 Proposed Amendment to Approved Free-Range Broiler Poultry Farm – Lot 13 Northam-York Road, Muluckine That Council:
1. ACCEPTS that Development Application P17038.2 is appropriate for consideration in accordance with clause 77 of the deemed provisions under the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
2. APPROVES Development Application P17038.2 and accompanying plans, in accordance with clause 77 of the deemed provisions under the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015 and the provisions of the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6, to amend the approved Free-Range Poultry Broiler Farm at Lot 87 Northam-York Road, Muluckine by:
a. increasing the number of sheds on Farm 1 from 6 to 8;
b. increasing the number of sheds on Farm 3 from 6 to 8; and
c. removing Farm 2 from the approved plan of development.
3. NOTES that all other conditions and requirements of the Development Approval dated 26 May 2017, as amended by the Development Approval dated 22 February 2022, shall remain applicable unless altered by this approval and the total number of approved poultry sheds remains at 16.
C.5645 13.3.3 Corporate Climate Mitigation and Adaptation Strategy That Council ADOPTS the Corporate Climate Mitigation and Adaptation Strategy and incorporated Target Action Plan as presented in Attachment 13.3.3.1.
C.5646 13.3.4 Development Application P26062 - 50 Wellington Street, Northam - Veterinary Centre That Council APPROVES the development application (Ref: P26062) for the change of use to a 'veterinary centre' at 50 Wellington Street, Northam, subject to the following conditions:

1. The development hereby approved must be substantially commenced within two (2) years from the date of determination.
2. The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the stamped approved plans of development.
3. Prior to occupation or use of the development, a vehicle crossover shall be constructed to the specifications and satisfaction of the local government.
4. The information displayed on the approved advertising signage must relate to the use being undertaken on the property.
5. The advertising signage shall not be illuminated or contain any flashing or moving lights at any time.
6. Prior to occupation or use of the development, the car parking bays (including universally accessible disabled bays), loading areas, vehicle access and circulation areas shown on the approved plans, shall be constructed, drained, and line marked and thereafter maintained to the specifications and satisfaction of the local government.
7. The use of the premises is to be for the purpose of ‘veterinary centre’, as defined in the Shire of Northam’s Local Planning Scheme No. 6 as follows:
‘“Veterinary Centre” means premises used to diagnose animal diseases or disorders, to surgically or medically treat animals, or for the prevention of animal diseases or disorders.’
A change of use from that outlined above may require the approval of the local government.
8. The stormwater shall be contained and managed on-site in a manner so that there is no discharge onto the adjoining properties to the specifications and satisfaction of the local government.
9. Prior to occupation or use of the development, a Final Acoustic Assessment must be prepared by a suitably qualified person and submitted to the local government for approval demonstrating that the development complies or will comply with the Environmental Protection (Noise) Regulations 1997. Any further works must be carried out in accordance with the approved Acoustic Report and implemented as such for the duration of the development.
10. Prior to occupation, the development shall be connected to an approved reticulated sewerage system.
11. Prior to occupation, the development shall be connected to an approved reticulated water supply.
12. Prior to commencement of any works, detailed designs for the location, materials and construction of bin areas, including screening shall be prepared to the specifications and satisfaction of the local government. Works may only commence following written approval of these detailed designs by the local government.
C.5647 13.4.1 Accounts & Statement of Accounts - August 2026 That Council RECEIVES the payments for the period 1 August to 31 August 2026, as listed:
• Municipal Fund BPay payment = $24,783.01
• Municipal Fund EFT payments = $1,686,727.87
• Direct Debits = $125,779.68
• Superannuation = $121,501.57
• Payroll = $657,732.53

TOTAL: $2,616,524.66

which have been made in accordance with the delegated authority reference number (M/F/F/Regs LGA 1995 S5.42).
C.5648 13.4.2 Monthly Financial Report for the period ending 31 July 2026 That Council:
1. RECEIVES the Monthly Financial Report, prepared in accordance with the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations, for the period ending 31 July 2026 presented as Attachment 13.4.2.1.
2. BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY APPROVES the amendments of revenue and expenditure in the 2026/27 budget as outlined in the table below: (see attached image)
C.5649 14 MATTERS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS That Council, in accordance with section 11.1(i) of the Shire of Northam Standing Orders Local Law 2018 and Section 5.23 (4)(b) of the Local Government Act 1995, meet behind closed doors to consider agenda item 14.1 - Legal Action for Recovery of Unpaid Rates as the matter relates to the personal affairs of a person.
C.5650 14.1 LEGAL ACTION FOR RECOVERY OF UNPAID RATES That Council AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to issue a Property Seizure and Sale Order on Goods and Land for A15155, in accordance with the Local Government Act 1995.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 19 August 2026

Wednesday, August 19, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 19 August 2026 at 5:30pm.

Click here to watch the live stream of the Council Meeting

Summary of Decisions:

Motion No. Item No Subject Motion
C.5614 10.1 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE ORDINARY COUNCIL MEETING HELD 29 JULY 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 29 July 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5615 10.2 NOTES FROM THE COUNCIL FORUM MEETING HELD 12 AUGUST 2026 That Council RECEIVES the notes from the Council Forum meeting held on Wednesday, 12 August 2026.
C.5616 13.1.1 Establishment of the Chief Executive Officer Selection Panel That Council:
1. ESTABLISHES the Chief Executive Officer Selection Panel under clause 8 of the Shire of Northam Standards for CEO Recruitment, Performance and Termination.
2. ADOPTS the Chief Executive Officer Selection Panel Terms of Reference contained in Attachment 13.1.1.1.
3. APPOINTS the following persons to the Chief Executive Officer Selection Panel:
a. Shire President C R Antonio, as Presiding Member;
b. Deputy Shire President A J Mencshelyi, as Deputy Presiding Member;
c. Cr M P Ryan;
d. Cr M I Girak;
e. Cr D A Hughes;
f. Cr J E G Williams;
g. Cr L C Biglin; and
h. Mr David Price, as the Independent Person.
4. APPOINTS McArthur as the recruitment consultant for the Chief Executive Officer recruitment and selection process for a fee of $18,500 plus GST and advertising expenses, in accordance with the quotation contained in confidential Attachment 13.1.1.5.
C.5617 13.3.1 Petition of Electors - Data Centres That Council:

1. NOTES the concerns raised in the petition regarding the development of data centres in Western Australia generally and within the Shire of Northam specifically.
2. DECLINES the request to prepare a public report identifying approved, proposed or publicly known data centre developments within the Shire - as it can be advised that there have been no applications for development approval for ‘data centres’ made to date, with only one ‘cryptocurrency mining facility’ granted development approval within the Shire of Northam.
3. DECLINES the request to conduct a public community forum on data centre developments within the Shire and the presenting of Council’s response to the issues and all requests raised in this petition, for the reasons outlined in this report.
4. DECLINES the request to develop a policy and/or initiate an amendment to the Local Planning Scheme and associated planning framework to require community consultation for future data centre developments where consultation is not otherwise required by the Planning and Development Act 2005 and the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
5. NOTES that any outcomes from Federal and/or State Government considerations regarding data centre developments that result in changes to Local Government planning frameworks and processes, including public consultation requirements will be adhered to by the Shire and on this basis, declines the request to write to the Minister for Planning seeking amendments to planning legislation and regulations to ensure public consultation occurs for major data centre developments.
6. DECLINES the request to review the development approval granted on 12 September 2025 for a crypto mining facility as a ‘warehouse’ land use at Lot 881 (No. 239) Yilgarn Avenue, Malabaine, as is compliant with the provisions of the Scheme and for the reasons outlined in this report.
7. DECLINES the request to reconsider or revoke the lawfully granted development approval issued on 12 September 2025 for a cryptocurrency mining facility as a ‘warehouse’ land use at Lot 881 (No. 239) Yilgarn Avenue, Malabaine, in the absence of proven unlawful development and/or non-compliance with conditions.
8. NOTES the request to publicly release documentation pertaining to applications for development approval that are not normally or typically made publicly available (e.g. as published on the Shire of Northam website) and REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to ascertain from the applicant what information, if any, they are prepared to make public in relation to the approved cryptocurrency mining facility. 
9. ADVISES that the Shire of Northam will continue to implement the Local Planning Strategy and administer its Local Planning Scheme in line with the adopted Council Plan priorities and projects, and in accordance with the Planning Development Act 2005 and associated Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
10. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to advise the lead petitioner of the outcome of the petition based on the recommendations in this report.
C.5618 13.3.2 Lot 22 Gaden Road, Wundowie That Council DEFERS the resubmitted Proposed Building Envelope Variation Plan dated 17 June 2026 as presented in Attachment 13.3.2.3 and subject to agenda item 13.3.2 Lot 22 Gaden Road, Wundowie, to allow further information to be submitted by the applicant, specifically with regards to the extent of vegetation modification, and/or removal on the property based on the proposed building footprints.
C.5619 13.3.3 Adoption of Scheme Amendment No. 26 That Council:

1. Pursuant to section 84 of the Planning and Development Act 2005 and in accordance with regulation 50(2) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, NOTES the submission received in respect to the proposed Scheme Amendment No. 26 to the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6 as considered, and ENDORSES the response to the submission as shown in the Schedule of Submissions at Attachment 13.3.3.3.
2. Pursuant to section 75 of the Planning and Development Act 2005 and in accordance with regulation 50(3)(b) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, DETERMINES to SUPPORT WITHOUT MODIFICATION Scheme Amendment No. 26 to the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6, as shown in Attachment 13.3.3.1, by:
(a) recoding the developable portion of Lot 9001 from a residential density code of ‘R15’ to 'R20’; and
(b) rezoning the balance of Lot 9001 from ‘Residential Zone’ to ‘Parks and Recreation Reserve’.
3. Pursuant to section 87 of the Planning and Development Act 2005 and in accordance with Regulation 53(1) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, SUBMITS the proposed amendment documentation without modification to the Western Australian Planning Commission, for the approval of the Minister for Planning.
4. AUTHORISES the Shire President and the Chief Executive Officer, in accordance with section 9.49a of the Local Government Act 1995, to execute under Common Seal affixed to the amending pages of Scheme Amendment No. 26 to Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6.
C.5620 13.4.1 Accounts & Statement of Accounts - July 2026 That Council RECEIVES the payments for the period 1 July to 31 July 2026, as listed:

• Municipal Fund payment cheque number 000113 = $13,972.20
• Municipal Fund EFT payment = $1,467,603.51
• Direct Debits = $551,922.34
• Superannuation = $165,830.77
• Payroll = $884,529.20

TOTAL: $3,083,858.02

which have been made in accordance with the delegated authority reference number (M/F/F/Regs LGA 1995 S5.42).
C.5621 13.4.2 Financial Statements for the period ending 30 June 2026 That Council:
1. RECEIVES the Financial Statements, prepared in accordance with the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations, for the period ending 30 June 2026 included as Attachment 13.4.2.1.
2. BY ASBOLUTE MAJORITY APPROVES the amendment of the capital expenses and grant revenue for road projects in the 2026/27 budget as outlined below (see attachment)
C.5622 13.4.3 Wheatbelt Rail Trail That Council:
1. SUPPORTS the Wheatbelt Rail Trails report as presented in Attachment 13.4.3.1;
2. PARTNERS with the other Local Governments on the Wheatbelt Rail Trails route to progress the actions contained in this report, subject to no financial commitment being made without further Council resolution; and
3. ENDORSES the Chief Executive Officer working with other relevant Local Governments to advocate for State and Federal Government funding to progress the Wheatbelt Rail Trails project.
C.5623 14 MATTERS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS That Council, in accordance with section 11.1(i) of the Shire of Northam Standing Orders Local Law 2018 and Section 5.23 (4)(b) of the Local Government Act 1995, meet behind closed doors to consider agenda item 14.1 - Legal Action for Recovery of Unpaid Rates as the item relates to the personal affairs of an individual.
C.5624 14.1 LEGAL ACTION FOR RECOVERY OF UNPAID RATES That Council:
1. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to issue a Property Seizure and Sale Order on Goods and Land for A10840, in accordance with the Local Government Act 1995.
2. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to issue a Property Seizure and Sale Order on Goods and Land for A12705, in accordance with the Local Government Act 1995.
3. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to issue a Property Seizure and Sale Order on Goods and Land for A11054, in accordance with the Local Government Act 1995
C.5625 14 MATTERS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS That Council move out from behind closed doors.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 29 July 2026

Wednesday, July 29, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 29 July 2026 at 5:30pm.

Summary of Agenda Items:

Motion No. Item No Subject Motion
C.5582 10.1 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE ORDINARY COUNCIL MEETING HELD 17 JUNE 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 17 June 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5583 10.2 NOTES FROM THE COUNCIL FORUM MEETING HELD 22 JULY 2026 That Council RECEIVES the notes from the Council Forum meeting held on Wednesday, 22 July 2026.
C.5584 10.3 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING HELD 8 JULY 2026 That the minutes of the Special Council meeting held on Wednesday, 8 July 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5585 13.1.1 Western Australian Local Government Association (WALGA) - Annual General Meeting That Council:
1. NOMINATES the Shire President and Cr J E G Williams as voting delegates at the 2026 Western Australian Local Government Association Annual General Meeting; and
2. NOMINATES Cr M  P Ryan as a proxy voting delegate at the 2026 Western Australian Local Government Association Annual General Meeting; and
3. DOES NOT submit a Member Motion to the 2026 Western Australian Local Government Association Annual General Meeting.
C.5586 13.1.2 Lease of Village Green - Lot 14, 174 Fitzgerald St, Northam That Council APPROVES entering into a new lease agreement with Malinowski Holdings Pty Ltd for 174 Fitzgerald Street, Northam (Lot 14) for the purpose of public open space, on the following terms:
a. Five (5) year lease term;
b. Option to renew for a further five (5) years;
c. Initial rent of $1,400.00 per calendar month plus GST;
d. Annual rent increases of 3% for the duration of the initial term;
e. A market rent review to be undertaken at the expiry of the initial term prior to exercising the option; and
f. All other terms and conditions consistent with the existing lease agreement provided in Attachment 13.1.2.1.
C.5587 13.3.1 Review of Local Planning Policy 24 - Outbuildings in the Rural Residential, Rural Smallholding & Rural Zones That Council:
1. Pursuant to Schedule 2, Part 2, Clause 4 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, ADOPTS the draft Local Planning Policy No. 24 – Outbuildings in the Rural Residential, Rural Smallholding and Rural Zones, as referenced in Attachment 13.3.1.2, for the purpose of public advertising;
2. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to undertake public advertising of the draft Local Planning Policy No. 24 for a minimum period of 21 days and invite submissions from the public and relevant stakeholders; and
3. RECEIVES a further report following the advertising period detailing any submissions received and seeking Council's consideration of the final adoption of Local Planning Policy No. 24.
C.5588 13.3.2 Review of Local Planning Policy 19 - Residential Design Guidelines for the Rural Residential & Rural Smallholding Zones That Council:
1. Pursuant to Schedule 2, Part 2, Clause 4 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, ADOPTS the draft Local Planning Policy No. 19 – Residential Design Guidelines for the Rural Residential and Rural Smallholding Zones as contained in Attachment 13.3.2.2 for the purpose of public advertising;
2. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to undertake public advertising of the draft Local Planning Policy No. 19 – Residential Design Guidelines for the Rural Residential and Rural Smallholding Zones for a minimum period of 21 days; and
3. RECEIVES a further report following the advertising period detailing any submissions received and seeking Council's consideration of the final adoption of Local Planning Policy No. 19.
C.5589 13.3.3 Revocation of Local Planning Policy No. 10 – Developments Abutting Rights of Way That Council:
1. Pursuant to clause 4 under Schedule 2 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, REVOKES Local Planning Policy No. 10 – Developments Abutting Rights of Way; and
2. NOTES that public advertising is not required for the revocation of this Local Planning Policy.
C.5590 13.3.4 Revocation of Local Planning Policy No. 8 – Retrospective Planning Applications and Fees That Council:
1. Pursuant to clause 4 under Schedule 2 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, REVOKES Local Planning Policy No. 8 – Retrospective Planning Applications and Fees; and
2. NOTES that public advertising is not required for the revocation of this Local Planning Policy.
C.5591 13.3.5 Renewal of Local Planning Policy No. 26 – Container Deposit Infrastructure That Council:
1. Pursuant to Clause 4 of Schedule 2 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, RESOLVES to renew Local Planning Policy No. 26 – Container Deposit Infrastructure without amendment, with the exception of an updated resolution date and scheduled review date as contained in Attachment 13.3.5.1.
2. NOTES that as there are no amendments to the actual content of Local Planning Policy 26, no public advertising is proposed.
C.5592 13.3.6 Brown Road Emergency Accessway That Council RESOLVES to retain the gates on the PAW located between Brown Road and Olive Road, Wundowie in an unlocked state.
C.5593 13.3.7 Bush Fire Advisory Committee Recommendations That Council:
1. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to investigate the legislative and administrative mechanisms available to allow the burning of 1 cubic metre piles, without the requirement for a burning permit during the latter stages of the Autumn Restricted Burning Period.
2. APPOINTS the following individuals for the 2026/27 and 2027/28 fire seasons:
a. Chief Bush Fire Control Officer
i. Mr Justin Fox
b. Deputy Chief Bush Fire Control Officers
i. Mr Kristafer Brown
ii. Mr Thomas Blair Wilding
C.5594 13.4.1 Accounts & Statement of Accounts - June 2026 That Council RECEIVES the payments for the period 1 June to 30 June 2026, as listed below:

• Municipal Fund payment cheque number 104 to 111 = $63,134.41
• Municipal Fund EFT57749 to EFT58017 = $1,358,680.13
• Direct Debits = $243,395.28
• Superannuation = $111,821.57
• Payroll = $577,129.68

TOTAL: $2,354,161.07

that have been made in accordance with the delegated authority reference number (M/F/F/Regs LGA 1995 S5.42).

1. ADOPTS the following annual fees for payment of Council Members in lieu of individual meeting attendance fees, pursuant to section 5.99 of the Local Government Act 1995, and within the range determined by the Salaries and Allowances Tribunal:
a. President $23,600
b. Councillors $20,198.25
2. ADOPTS the following annual Information & Communication
3. Technology (ICT) expenses allowance for Council Members, pursuant to section 5.99A of the Local Government Act 1995 and within the
4. range determined by the Salaries and Allowances Tribunal:
a. ICT Expenses Allowance $2,786.84

a. President $45,000
6. ADOPTS, pursuant to section 5.98A of the Local Government Act 1995
7. and within the range determined by the Salaries and Allowances
8. Tribunal, the following annual local government allowance to be paid in addition to the annual meeting allowance:
a. Deputy President $11,250
C.5596 13.4.3 Budget Adoption 2026/28 That Council, by ABSOLUTE MAJORITY, ADOPTS the following Kerbside Waste Collection Charges for the 2026/27 financial year as outlined in Attachment 13.4.2.1:

a) General Waste Kerbside Collection – Residential $238.00
b) Recycling Kerbside Collection – Residential  $122.00
c) Pensioner Recycling Kerbside Collection – Residential  $99.00

h) 1500L Commercial Recycling Bin (fortnightly)  $1,526.00
i) 3000L Commercial General Waste Bin (weekly) $2,776.00

n) 4500L Commercial Recycling Bin (fortnightly) $4,577.00
C.5597 13.4.4 Budget Adoption 2026/29 That Council, by ABSOLUTE MAJORITY, for the 2026/27 financial year:
1. IMPOSES, pursuant to sections 6.32, 6.33, 6.34 and 6.35 of the Local
2. Government Act 1995, the following differential general and minimum rates on Gross Rental and Unimproved Values for the 2026/27 financial year for the purpose of yielding the deficiency disclosed by the Municipal Fund Budget in recommendation 6:
 
a. Differential General Rates
i. Residential (GRV) 11.6850 cents in the dollar

b. Minimum Rates

2. OFFERS, pursuant to section 6.45 of the Local Government Act 1995 and regulation 64(2) of the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 1996, a one, two and four instalment payment option, and sets the following due dates for the payment in full by instalments:
a. Full payment & 1st instalment due date 18 September 2026

C.5598 13.4.5 Budget Adoption 2026/30 That Council, by ABSOLUTE MAJORITY, ADOPTS the amended Schedule of Fees and Charges for 2026/27 financial year as contained in Attachment 13.4.2.1.
C.5599 13.4.6 Budget Adoption 2026/31 That Council, by ABSOLUTE MAJORITY, in accordance with regulation 34(5) of the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 1996, and AASB 1031 Materiality, APPROVES that the level to be used in statements of financial activity in 2026/27 for reporting material variances shall be a percentage of 10 or a minimum of $20,000, whichever is greater.
C.5600 13.4.7 Budget Adoption 2026/32 That Council, by ABSOLUTE MAJORITY, pursuant to the provisions of section 6.2 of the Local Government Act 1995 and Part 3 of the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 1996, ADOPTS the Municipal Fund Budget as contained in Attachments 13.4.2.4 for the Shire of Northam for the 2026/27 financial year and amended to include the new rates model.
C.5601 14 MATTERS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS That Council, in accordance with section 11.1(i) of the Shire of Northam Standing Orders Local Law 2018 and Section 5.23 (2)(b)(ii) & (4)(b) of the Local Government Act 1995, meet behind closed doors to consider agenda items:
• 14.1 - Clackline Fire Shed Access – Lots 750, 199 Gooch Road, Mokine as the matter relates to the personal affairs of an individual;
• 14.2 - Legal Action for Recovery of Unpaid Rates as the matter relates to the personal affairs of an individual;
• 14.3 - Sale of Land for Recovery of Unpaid Rates as the matter relates to the personal affairs of an individual;
• 14.4 - Rates Exemption Application as the matter relates to the personal affairs of an individual;

• 14.6 - Minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Review Committee held 17 June 2026 as the matter relates to the employment of the CEO; and
• 14.7 - Minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Review Committee held 22 July 2026 as the matter relates to the employment of the CEO.
C.5602 14.1 CLACKLINE FIRE SHED ACCESS – LOTS 750, 199 GOOCH ROAD, MOKINE That Council:
1. APPROVES the creation of an easement over the portion of land at Lot 750 (199 Gooch Road, Mokine) adjacent to Reserve 3214 for the purpose of providing ongoing access to the Clackline Fire Shed.
2. AUTHORISES the payment of compensation of $8,000 to the landowner of A662, together with all reasonable costs associated with the survey, preparation, lodgement and registration of the easement.
3. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to negotiate the final terms of the easement and execute all necessary documentation to give effect to the easement.

4. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to issue a Property Seizure and Sale Order on Goods and Land for A13089, in accordance with the Local Government Act 1995.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 17 June 2026

Wednesday, June 17, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 17 June 2026 at 5:30pm.

Summary of Decision(s): 

Motion No. Item No. Subject Motion
C.5563 8 Petitions That Council:
1. RECEIVES the petition submitted to the Shire in relation to Data Centres; and
2. REFERS the petition to the Chief Executive Officer for consideration in accordance with clause 6.10 of the Shire of Northam Standing Orders Amendment Local Law 2018.
C.5564 10.1 Confirmation of Minutes from the Ordinary Council Meeting held 27 May 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 27 May 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5565 10.2 Notes from the Council Forum Meeting held 10 June 2026 That Council RECEIVES the notes from the Council Forum meeting held on Wednesday, 10 June 2026.
C.5566 12.1 Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee Meeting held on 19 May 2026 That Council RECEIVES the minutes from the Audit, Risk & Improvement Committee meeting held on 19 May 2026.
C.5567 12.1 Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee Meeting held on 19 May 2026 That Council:
1. NOTES the information contained in Attachment 7.1.1 in relation to the 2025/26 audit for the Shire of Northam to be conducted by Pitcher Partners on behalf of the Office of the Auditor General.
2. ENDORSES the revised ICT Disaster Recovery Plan 2026 - 2028 as presented in Attachment 7.2.1.
3. NOTES the requirement to continue investing in backup solutions and testing to ensure timely data recovery and business continuity in the event of a system failure, cyber incident or other disruptive events.
4. RECEIVES the Internal Reviews and Audit Actions update as presented in Attachments 7.3.1 and 7.3.2.
5. RECEIVES the update as provided in Attachment 7.4.3 in relation to the progress made towards implementation of the ICT Strategy Plan.
6. NOTES the measures outlined in the report to manage the ERP project delivery risks including additional project phasing, extended delivery timeframes and engagement of external resourcing to assist with implementation.
7. RECEIVES the May 2026 update on the Shire of Northam Strategic Risk Register.
8. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to implement the changes proposed in this report, specifically in relation to “R00070 – Impact of Climate Change and Environmental Management”.
9. RECEIVES the February 2026 to April 2026 update on the internal compliance checks as provided in Attachment 7.6.1.
10. RECEIVES the May 2026 update as provided in Attachment 7.7.1 in relation to the progress made towards the Privacy and Responsible Information Sharing (PRIS) Action Plan.
11. NOTES the update regarding Rates debt and Sundry debt and associated recovery actions being pursued as outlined in confidential Attachments 7.8.1 to 7.8.3.
C.5568 13.1.1 Major Review - Council Plan 2026-2036 That the following words be added after "1. ADOPTS the Shire of Northam Council Plan 2026-2036, as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.2, as the Shire’s integrated Strategic Community Plan and Corporate Business Plan for the district in accordance with section 5.56 of the Local Government Act 1995 and regulations 19C and 19DA of the Local Government (Administration) Regulations 1996":

"subject to the following amendment:

that Item 7.2.6 be amended to read: "Finalise delivery of the Wundowie Community Hub and Water Park Feasibility Study and retain the Wundowie Community Hub as a strategic priority, with future planning informed by the outcomes of the study."; and
that Item 7.2.6 be identified as "Additional funding to be determined" for 2026/27, 2027/28, 2028/29 and 2029/30."
C.5569 13.1.1 Major Review - Council Plan 2026-2036 That Council:
1. ADOPTS the Shire of Northam Council Plan 2026-2036, as provided in Attachment 13.1.1.2, as the Shire’s integrated Strategic Community Plan and Corporate Business Plan for the district in accordance with section 5.56 of the Local Government Act 1995 and regulations 19C and 19DA of the Local Government (Administration) Regulations 1996, subject to the following amendment:
a. that Item 7.2.6 be amended to read: "Finalise delivery of the Wundowie Community Hub and Water Park Feasibility Study and retain the Wundowie Community Hub as a strategic priority, with future planning informed by the outcomes of the study."; and
b. that Item 7.2.6 be identified as "Additional funding to be determined" for 2026/27, 2027/28, 2028/29 and 2029/30.
2. NOTES that the updated inserts provided in Attachment 13.1.1.1 will be incorporated into the designed Council Plan provided at Attachment 13.1.1.2.
3. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to make minor editorial, formatting and design amendments to the Council Plan 2026-2036 before publication, provided those amendments do not materially alter the intent, priorities or financial allocations adopted by Council.
4. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to give local public notice of the adoption of the Council Plan 2026-2036 and publish the adopted Plan on the Shire’s website.
C.5570 13.1.2 Northam Airfield Management Agreement That Council:
1. APPROVES continuation of the operational management arrangement for the Northam Airfield with Northam Aero Club Inc. for a five (5) year term commencing 1 July 2026 and expiring 30 June 2031, with one further five (5) year renewal option available by agreement of the parties;
2. APPROVES the annual management fee for the first year of the renewed Management Agreement being set at $12,618.80, consistent with the 2025/26 management fee, with future annual fee adjustments to be applied in accordance with the terms of the renewed Management Agreement;
3. REQUIRES that the renewed Management Agreement be on terms and conditions consistent with the Management Agreement expiring on 30 June 2026, subject to any administrative, statutory or operational amendments acceptable to the Chief Executive Officer; and
4. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to negotiate and execute the renewed Management Agreement with Northam Aero Club Inc. for the operational management of the Northam Airfield.
C.5571 13.1.3 Reserve 43257, Garrigan Close, Northam That Council:
1. CONSENTS to the creation of an easement over Reserve 43257 (Lot 29137 on Plan 17921) in favour of the owners of Lot 801 on Deposited Plan 400751 for the purpose of constructing and maintaining a water pipeline, substantially in accordance with the plan shown in Attachment 13.1.3.1;
2. NOTES that the easement is subject to approval by the Minister for Lands and completion of all requirements of the Department of Planning, Lands and Heritage, as outlined in Attachment 13.1.3.5; and
3. REQUIRES that all costs associated with the creation, registration and implementation of the easement are met by the applicant.
C.5572 13.1.4 Proposed Lease of Northam Airfield Hangar Sites 42-47 That Council:
1. DECLARES, for the purposes of section 3.58(4)(c)(ii) of the Local Government Act 1995, that the valuation obtained on 7 April 2022 for the Northam Airfield hangar sites is believed to be a true indication of the current market value of the proposed disposition, noting the valuation informed the commercial hangar site tenancy fee adopted in Council Policy CP.58 Property Management (Leases and Licences) and the Shire’s Schedule of Fees and Charges.
2. APPROVES local public notice being given, in accordance with section 3.58 of the Local Government Act 1995, of the proposed disposition of Hangar Sites 42, 43, 44, 45, 46 and 47, located at 105 Withers Street, Northam, by lease to Helispecs Aviation Pty Ltd.
3. APPROVES the proposed lease being advertised on the following key terms:
a. lessee: Helispecs Aviation Pty Ltd;
b. property: Hangar Sites 42, 43, 44, 45, 46 and 47, 105 Withers Street, Northam;
c. total lease area: 2,064m²;
d. permitted use: commercial aviation purposes;
e. annual lease fee: $12,384 excluding GST, calculated at the commercial hangar site tenancy fee of $6.00 per m² per annum;
f. lease term: expiring on 30 June 2035;
g. renewal option: one further term of five years;
h. lease preparation costs: payable by the lessee, currently approximately $1,100 as invoiced by the Shire;
i. outgoings, improvements, repairs, maintenance and relevant statutory approvals: responsibility of the lessee; and
j. special condition: the lessee must obtain development approval for the proposed hangar development within 12 months of the lease being executed.
4. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer, subject to no significant submissions being received during the public notice period, to negotiate, finalise and execute the lease with Helispecs Aviation Pty Ltd generally in accordance with the terms outlined in this report.
5. REQUIRES that if significant submissions are received during the public notice period, the matter be referred to Council for further consideration before the proposed disposition proceeds.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 27 May 2026

Wednesday, May 27, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 27 May 2026 at 5:30pm.

Summary of Decisions:

Motion no. Item No. Subject Motion
C.5540 9 APPLICATIONS FOR LEAVE OF ABSENCE That Council GRANTS Cr M I Girak leave of absence from 4 July 2026 to 31 July 2026 (inclusive).
C.5541 9 APPLICATIONS FOR LEAVE OF ABSENCE That Council GRANTS Cr D A Hughes leave of absence from 21 July 2026 to 28 July 2026 (inclusive).
C.5542 10.1 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE ORDINARY COUNCIL MEETING HELD 22 APRIL 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 22 April 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5543 10.2 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING HELD 13 MAY 2026 That the minutes of the Special Council Meeting held on Wednesday, 13 May 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5544 10.3 NOTES FROM THE COUNCIL FORUM MEETING HELD 20 MAY 2026 That Council RECEIVES the notes from the Council Forum meeting held on Wednesday, 20 May 2026.
C.5545 13.3.3 Future Direction of Visitor Servicing That the following words be added after the words "2. INVESTIGATES options for future use of the Northam Visitor Centre facility located at 2 Grey Street, Northam":

3. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to explore future options, in conjunction with the Northam Army Camp Heritage Association and the Avon Valley Arts Society, for the Sense of Place exhibition and the Avon Valley Arts Society items currently displayed in the Visitors Centre.
C.5546 13.3.4 Future Direction of Visitor Servicing That Council:
1. ENDORSES Option 1 being the permanent colocation of visitor servicing operations at the Bilya Koort Boodja Centre for Nyoongar Culture and Environmental Knowledge.
2. INVESTIGATES options for future use of the Northam Visitor Centre facility located at 2 Grey Street, Northam.
3. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to explore future options, in conjunction with the Northam Army Camp Heritage Association and the Avon Valley Arts Society, for the Sense of Place exhibition and the Avon Valley Arts Society items currently displayed in the Visitors Centre.
C.5547 13.1.3 Lease of Morby Cottage & the former Mayors Parlour That Council REVOKE decision C.4762 which was made at the Ordinary Council Meeting held on 21 June 2023.
C.5548 13.1.4 Lease of Morby Cottage & the former Mayors Parlour That Council:
1. APPROVES a non-exclusive licence for a term of ten (10) years, with a ten (10) year renewal under Council Policy CP.58 – Property Management (Leases and Licences) to the Northam & Districts Historical Society for use of the following areas at the Northam Town Hall:
  • o Former Mayor’s Parlour
  • o Fenced storage area at the rear of the Town Hall
  • o Storage room within the Town Hall corridor
2. DETERMINES that:
  • o document preparation costs are waived; and
  • o utilities and outgoings are met by the Shire.
3. REQUIRES the licensee to maintain public liability and contents insurance.
4. SETS the licence fee at $1 per annum, with the Shire responsible for building insurance.
5. NOTES that the Morby Cottage lease extension option to 30 November 2027 will be exercised under delegated authority following revocation of decision C.4762.
C.5549 13.3.2 Proposed Scheme Amendment 25 - Omnibus Amendment

That Council:

  1. RESOLVES, pursuant to section 75 of the Planning and Development Act 2005 and regulations 35 and 46A of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, to initiate an amendment to the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6, by:
  1. Updating PART 1 - PRELIMINARY in accordance with the Schedule 1 – Model provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, but retaining content of clause 1.4 (c) and the existing scheme aims.
  2. Updating PART 2 – RESERVES in accordance with the Schedule 1 – Model provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, including the inserting of model provision reserves in accordance with clause 1 of Schedule 3 for reserve legends used in local planning scheme maps.
  3. Updating PART 3 – ZONES and the Use of Land in accordance with the Schedule 1 – Model provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
  4. Updating of TABLE 1: ZONING TABLE with the rationalisation of land use classes, both deleted and added, and their associated level of permissibility.
  5. Updating PART 4 – GENERAL DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS in accordance with the Schedule 1 – Model provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
  6. Deleting clauses 4.1 to 4.7 and replace with Schedule 1 – Model provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
  7. Revising of existing clause 4.11 RETAINING WALLS in respect to development for which the R-Codes do not apply.
  8. Updating of clause 4.13 CAR PARKING and TABLE 3: CAR PARKING GUIDELINES in line with the updated ZONING TABLE.
  9. Inserting of subclause 4.21.3 under clause 4.21 HOME OCCUPATION, HOME BUSINESS AND RURAL HOME BUSINESS.
  10. Amending clause 4.22 OUTBUILDINGS by deleting subclause 4.22.1 and adding ‘Commercial’, ‘Mixed Use’ and ‘Rural’ to the zones listed in subclause 4.22.3.
  11. Inserting of subclause 4.25.4 under clause 4.25 EXTRACTIVE AND MINING INDUSTRIES.
  12. Replacing of subclause 4.30.1 under clause 4.30 DEVELOPMENT IN THE RURAL ZONE.
  13. Amending the provisions of clause 4.31 DEVELOPMENT IN THE RURAL RESIDENTIAL AND RURAL SMALLHOLDING ZONES.
  14. Deleting the entirety of clauses 4.34 OCCUPANCY OF CARAVAN PARKS AND PARK HOME PARKS, 4.35 TELECOMMUNICATIONS INFRASTRUCTURE and 4.36 HOME OFFICE, HOME OCCUPATION AND HOME BUSINESS and renumbering the remaining clauses in Part 4.
  15. Amending the heading of clause 4.33 REPURPOSED AND SECOND-HAND DWELLING AND BUILDINGS to read ‘RE-PURPOSED AND SECOND-HAND DWELLINGS’, and revising the subclauses with correct and consistent numbering.
  16. Deleting clause 4.38 STATE PLANNING POLICY 3.6 TO BE READ AS PART OF SCHEME, in accordance with Planning and Development (State Planning Policies) Regulations 2024, and renumbering the remaining clauses in Part 4.
  17. Inserting of new clause 4.39 PUBLIC OPEN SPACE CONTRIBUTIONS FOR INFILL RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT, in line with WAPC Position Statement: Public Open Space (19 December 2025), and renumbering the remaining clauses in Part 4.
  18. Updating PART 5 – SPECIAL CONTROL AREAS in accordance with the Schedule 1 – Model provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
  19. Inserting of PART 6 – TERMS REFERRED TO IN SCHEME as per the Schedule 1 – Model provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, replacing the content of deleted SCHEDULE 1 – DICTIONARY OF DEFINED WORDS AND EXPRESSIONS.
  20. Modifying of the entries in the table under SCHEDULE 2 – ADDITIONAL USES by deleting, amending and inserting of new additional uses and associated conditions, as renumbered.
  21. Modifying of the entries in the table under SCHEDULE 4 – SPECIAL USE ZONES by deleting, amending and inserting of new special uses and associated conditions, as renumbered.
  22. Under SCHEDULE 7 – RURAL RESIDENTIAL ZONES and SCHEDULE 8 – RURAL SMALLHOLDINGS ZONES, as renumbered, inserting ‘Hosted Short-Term Rental Accommodation (P)’ under the land uses listed in the conditions column for RR2, RR3, RR4, RR6, RR8, RR11, RR12, RR13, RR15, RR24, RR25, RR26, RR27, RSH1 and RSH4.
  23. Amending SCHEDULE A – SUPPLEMENTAL PROVISIONS TO THE DEEMED PROVISIONS to align with the format of Schedule 2 – Deemed provisions of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
  24. Updating of the Scheme Map sheets in accordance with the relevant amendments itemised above, including changes to zone and reserve names and notations in accordance with Schedule 1 and Schedule 3 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, and by making the following changes below:

(see page 383 of the attached Minutes for further table)

2. NUMBER the proposed local planning scheme amendment as ‘Amendment No. 25’ to the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6.

3. DETERMINES, pursuant to regulation 35(2) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, that the amendment is a standard amendment for the following reasons:


c.  it is consistent with the intent of the Shire of Northam Local Planning Strategy (2024);

d.  it responds to legislative and policy reforms made at the State level, in particular to be more consistent with the model provisions in Schedule 1, deemed provisions in Schedule 2, and scheme map legends used in Schedule 3 of the Regulations;

e.  it makes corrections to administrative errors or omissions in the Scheme Text and on Scheme Map sheets;

f.  it will have limited to no material impact on land that is subject to the amendment; and

g.  it will not result in significant negative environmental, social, economic or governance impacts on land in the Scheme area that is not subject to the amendment.

4. Pursuant to section 81 of the Planning and Development Act 2005, refers the proposed Amendment No. 25 to the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) prior to advertising in accordance with regulation 47 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.
 

5. Subject to section 83A of the Planning and Development Act 2005 and regulation 46B of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, advertise Amendment No. 25 for a minimum period of 42 days, in accordance with section 84 of the Act and regulation 47 of the Regulations.
 

6. Compile any resulting comments or modifications to be further considered by Council pursuant to clause 87 of the Planning and Development Act 2005 and regulation 50 of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 22 April 2026

Wednesday, April 22, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 22 April 2026 at 5:30pm.

Summary of Decision(s):

Motion No. Item No Subject Motion
C.5523 14.9 MATTERS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS That Council move out from behind closed doors. Forum
C.5524 9.1 Applications for Leave of Absence That Council GRANTS Cr J E G Williams leave of absence from 21 May 2026 to 4 June 2026 (inclusive)
C.5525 10.1 Confirmation of Minutes from the Ordinary Council Meeting held 25 March 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 25 March 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5526 10.2 Notes from the Council Forum Meeting held 15 April 2026 That Council RECEIVES the notes from the Council Forum meeting held on Wednesday, 15 April 2026.
C.5527 12.1 Community Grants Assessment Committee Meeting Held 8 APRIL 2026 That Council RECEIVES the minutes from the Community Grants Assessment Committee meeting held on 8 April 2026.
C.5528 12.1 Community Grants Assessment Committee Meeting Held 8 APRIL 2026 That Council APPROVES the Community Event annual allocations for a 3-year funding agreement commencing in 2026/27 as follows:

  1. Up to $15,000 per annum (excluding GST) to the Northam Agricultural Society for the Northam Farmers Show.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 25 March 2026

Wednesday, March 25, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 25 March 2026 at 5:30pm.

Summary of Decisions:

Motion No. Item No Subject Motion
C.5506 9 APPLICATIONS FOR LEAVE OF ABSENCE That Council GRANT Cr A J Mencshelyi leave of absence from 13 April 2026 to 23 April 2026 (inclusive).
C.5507 10.1 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES FROM THE ORDINARY COUNCIL MEETING HELD 25 FEBRUARY 2026 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 25 February 2026 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5508 10.2 NOTES FROM THE COUNCIL FORUM MEETING HELD 18 MARCH 2026 That Council RECEIVE the notes from the Council Forum meeting held on Wednesday, 18 March 2026.
C.5509 12.1 MINUTES FROM THE AUDIT, RISK AND IMPROVEMENT COMMITTEE MEETING HELD ON 17 FEBRUARY 2026 That Council RECEIVES the minutes from the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee meeting held on 17 February 2026.
C.5510 12.1 MINUTES FROM THE AUDIT, RISK AND IMPROVEMENT COMMITTEE MEETING HELD ON 17 FEBRUARY 2027

That Council:

  1. ADOPTS CP.21 Fraud and Corruption Control as detailed in Attachment 7.1.1 to this Report.
  2. NOTES the Integrity Snapshot Tool and Integrity Framework Maturity Self-Assessment, as detailed in Attachment 7.1.4 and 7.1.5 to this Report.
  3. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to report progress against actions arising from the Integrity Snapshot Tool and Integrity Framework Maturity Self-Assessment to the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee on a quarterly basis until all actions are complete.
  4. ADOPTS the Fraud and Corruption Control Plan as detailed in Attachment 7.1.3 to this report.
  5. RECEIVES the Internal Reviews and Audit Actions update as presented in Attachments 7.2.1.
  6. RECEIVES the update as provided in Attachment 7.3.1 in relation to the progress made towards implementation of the ICT Strategy Plan.
  7. NOTES the measures outlined in the report to manage the ERP project delivery risks including additional project phasing, extended delivery timeframes and engagement of external resourcing to assist with implementation.
  8. RECEIVES the February 2026 update on the Shire of Northam Strategic Risk Register.
  9. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to implement the changes proposed under the “Strategic Risk Register Review Outcomes” of this report specifically in relation to R00069 – Insufficient External Funding for Core Service Delivery and R00070 – Impact of Climate Change and Environmental Management.
  10. RECEIVES the November 2025 to January 2026 update on the internal compliance checks as provided in Attachments 7.5.1 to 7.5.7.
  11. RECEIVES the February 2026 update as provided in Attachment 7.6.1 in relation to the progress made towards the Privacy and Responsible Information Sharing (PRIS) Action Plan.
  12. NOTES the identified need for additional resourcing to assist the Shire in preparing for the PRIS legislation and a proposal for funding being included in the 2025/26 Budget Review process.
  13. NOTES the findings of the October 2025 assessment undertaken by the Aged Care Quality and Safety Committee of the services provided at the Killara Adult Day and Respite Centre against the Aged Care Quality and Safety Standards as documented in Attachment 7.7.1 of this Report.
  14. ENDORSES implementation of the corrective actions as documented in Attachment 7.7.2 to this Report that are intended to address the findings of the assessment.
  15. NOTES the Fraud and Corruption Control update and the actions taken by the Chief Executive Officer.
C.5511 13.1.1 Sector Consultation - Electoral Reform Discussion Paper

That Council:

  1. ENDORSES the proposed responses to the WALGA Electoral Reform Discussion Paper as contained within this report; and
  2. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to submit the Council-endorsed responses to the Western Australian Local Government Association by the specified deadline.

·     brewery

Where a Local Development Plan (LDP) has been approved by the local government, the level of permissibility of the above listed special uses may be determined in accordance with the adopted LDP.

1General

1.1  The intent of the special use zone is to provide for a range of suitable tourism, mixed use, commercial, and light & service industry land use activities in a manner that:

(a)  provides for a high quality of amenity and urban design; and

(b)  does not give rise to any potential land use conflicts or have any detrimental impacts on road safety and the natural environment.

1.2  Access arrangements along the ‘Regional Road Reserve’ are to be to the specifications and satisfaction of Main Roads Western Australia (MRWA) and the local government.

1.3  Vehicle access, circulation and on-site parking provision for all land uses are to be in accordance with the Scheme, or as provided for in accordance with an adopted LDP.

1.4  The local government may require the preparation and submission of the following for its consideration and endorsement prior to the approval of any LDP and/or the granting of development approval:

(a)  Landscape Plan, inclusive of a Landscape Management Plan;

(b)  Stormwater Management Plan;

(c)  Transport Impact Assessment (TIA); and/or

(d)  Road Safety Audit (RSA).

1.5  Signage and advertising:

(a)  A precinct signage plan may be required by the local government to be submitted as part of any LDP, which is to regulate the location and area of signage, the type of signage, its unified style and quality of presentation.

(b)  Applications for development approval for the development of premises will require a detailed signage plan, which is to be approved by the local government, in consultation with MRWA, prior to commencement of works.

1.6  Shop use is limited to a maximum retail floorspace area of 1,500m² net lettable area (nla) for the entire special use zone area.*

2  Development Approval

2.1  All development and/or land use, including a change of use, shall be the subject of an application for development approval where proposed on land in the special use zone area in the absence of an approved LDP.

3  Site and Development Standards and Requirements

3.1  Subject to the discretion of the local government, in the absence of an approved LDP, the standards and requirements of land use and development of premises in the special use zone area is to be in accordance with the following:

(a)minimum boundary setback (metres):

front – 7.5m,

rear – 7.5m,

side – 4m; and

(b)minimum landscaping area of 10%.

4  Local Development Plan

4.1  A LDP, where proposed, is to be prepared for the entire special use zone area in accordance State Planning Policy 7.2 Precinct Design and approved in accordance with Part 6 of the Deemed Provisions.

4.2  Where a LDP has been approved by the local government, the extent and layout of land uses and the urban design of development is to be generally in accordance with the adopted LDP site and development standards and requirements.

4.3  The local government may choose to waive the requirement for a LDP where it is satisfied that:

(a)  proposed development does not conflict with the principles of orderly and proper planning; and

(b)  proposed development would not prejudice the overall development potential of the local area.

Wednesday, February 25, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Summary of Decisions:

That Council:

  1.   2. Pursuant to section 75 of the Planning and Development Act 2005, and in accordance with Regulation 50(3)(a) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, RESOLVES to support the proposed amendment without modification to the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6 by:
    1. Modifying Schedule 4 No.SU9 by inserting the following provisions:
      1. ‘At subdivision stage use restrictions shall be imposed on lots to limit occupancy to persons 45 years and older.’
      2. Inserting land use ‘Independent living complex’ to the special use column as well as, inserting ‘(D)’ after each of all the land use.
    2. Modifying Schedule 4 No.SU12 by deleting the following land use:
    3. ‘and Residential aged care facility and associated uses’.
    4. Modifying Schedule 4 No.SU12 by inserting the following land use:
      ‘Independent living complex (D)’
    5. Modifying Schedule 4 No.SU12 by deleting the following provisions:
      1.  ‘6. No development will be permitted within 500m of the Linley Valley abattoir and its associated wastewater ponds.’
      2.  ‘7. Construction of the residential aged care facility is to be substantially commenced prior to approval of the 41st lot in SU12.’

e. Modifying Schedule 4 No.SU12 by rewording the following provisions:

      1. ‘4. The R-Codes are to apply. Subdivision and development is to be in accordance with the R40 density code.’
      2. ‘9. (BMP provision) Include words ‘separation to any identified habitat protection areas’ after ‘siting and design’ and delete words ‘of development’.

f. Modifying Schedule 4 No.SU12 by inserting the following provisions:
‘Prior to any application for subdivision or development impacting native vegetation, a flora and fauna survey shall be conducted, inclusive of a black cockatoo habitat survey, to identify building exclusion areas for habitat protection.’

g. Modifying Schedule 1 – Dictionary of defined words and expressions of the Scheme by inserting the land use definition of:
“Independent living complex” means a development with self-contained, independent dwellings for aged or dependent persons together with communal amenities and facilities for residents and staff that are incidental and ancillary to the provision of such accommodation, but does not include a development which includes these features as a component of a residential aged care facility.

C.5496 13.3.3 Proposed Scheme Amendment 19 - 264 Chedaring Rd, Wundowie

That Council:

  1. Pursuant to section 84 of the Planning and Development Act 2005, and in accordance with Regulation 50(2) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, NOTES the submissions received in respect to the proposed Amendment No. 19 to the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6 and ENDORSES the response to the submissions as shown in the Schedule of Submissions at Attachment 13.3.2.5.
  2. Pursuant to section 75 of the Planning and Development Act 2005, and in accordance with Regulation 50(3)(b) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, RESOLVES to support the proposed amendment to the Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6, as modified in accordance with Department of Planning, Lands and Heritage requirements for consent to advertise under section 83A(2)(b) of the Act, by:
    1. Rezoning Lots 9000, 304 and 303 Chedaring Road, Wundowie from ‘Rural Zone’ to ‘Rural Residential Zone’ and ‘Environmental Conservation Zone’ and amend the scheme map accordingly.
    2. Modifying clause 4.37 – Development in Environmental Conservation Zone, by:
    3. Replacing subclause 4.37.2 with the following:
      4.37.2 Subdivision of Environmental Conservation zones will generally not be supported.
    4. Inserting the following new subclause 4.37.5:
      4.37.5 Development approval is required for all development within the Environmental Conservation zone.
    5. Inserting the following new subclause 4.37.6:
      4.37.6 Unless otherwise approved by the local government, all buildings and on-site effluent disposal systems shall be confined to the approved building envelope. Building envelopes and associated access and servicing infrastructure are to be located in areas assessed as having the poorest quality vegetation condition in the zone.
    6. Inserting a new entry ‘RR31’ into the table under Schedule 7 – Rural Residential Zones, as follows:
      No. Description of land Conditions
      RR31. Lots 9000, 303 and 304 (No. 264) Chedaring Road, Wundowie
      1. Subdivision and development is prohibiteduntil a structure plan is prepared andapproved.
      2.  Prior to the preparation of a structure plan,completion of flora and vegetation andterrestrial fauna surveys consistent with Environmental Protection Authority and/or other relevant technical guidance is required to identify conservation and significant environmental values, including:
        1. confirmation of areas containing vegetation representative of Eucalypt Woodlands of the Western Australian Wheatbelt Priority Ecological Community;
        2. black cockatoo foraging habitat assessment; and
        3. black cockatoo nesting tree and hollow assessment.
      3. The structure plan shall include and set out the outcomes of condition 2 in respect to avoidance (retention) and mitigation of potential impacts to significant environmental values.
      4. Prior to subdivision an Environmental Management Plan (EMP) shall be prepared to the satisfaction of the Shire of Northam, in consultation with the State government department responsible for biodiversity conservation. The EMP shall address as a minimum:
        1. outcomes of conditions 2 and 3 and actions to prevent and manage impacts of development on vegetation and fauna habitat identified for retention; and
        2. the management measures to ensure the habitat functions of these areas are maintained and, where possible, enhanced.
      5. Minimum lot sizes shall be 2ha.
      6. In implementing the requirements of conditions 2 to 5, lot sizes within RR31 may be larger than 4ha to accommodate the retention of environmental values or as site conditions require, as guided by an approved structure plan.
  3. Pursuant to section 87 of the Planning and Development Act 2005, and in accordance with Regulation 53(1) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, SUBMITS the proposed amendment documentation, as modified to accord with the advice of the Environmental Protection Authority, to the Western Australian Planning Commission, for the approval of the Minister.
  4. AUTHORISES the Shire President and the Chief Executive Officer, in accordance with section 9.49A of the Local Government Act 1995, to execute under Common Seal affixed to the amending pages of Scheme Amendment No. 19 to Shire of Northam Local Planning Scheme No. 6.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 28 January 2026

Wednesday, January 28, 2026 - 05:30 PM

Location: Shire of Northam Council Chambers

An Ordinary Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 28 January 2026 at 5:30pm.

Summary of Decisions:

Motion No. Item No. Subject Motion
C.5472 9.1 Applications for Leave of Absence That Council GRANTS Cr J E G Williams leave of absence from 20 March 2026 to 2 April 2026 (inclusive).
C.5473 10.1 Confirmation of Minutes from the Ordinary Council Meeting held 17 December 2025 That the minutes of the Ordinary Council meeting held on Wednesday, 17 December 2025 be CONFIRMED as a true and correct record of that meeting.
C.5474 13.1.1 Change of Council Meeting Date - June 2026 That Council:

1. APPROVES the change of date for the Council Forum Meeting from 17 June 2026 to 10 June 2026.

2. APPROVES the change of date for the Ordinary Council Meeting from 24 June 2026 to 17 June 2026.

3. REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to publish the change of meeting dates on the Shire of Northam website in accordance with Regulation 12 of the Local Government (Administration) Regulations 1996 and on the Shire’s social media platforms.
C.5475 13.2.1 RFT 10 of 2025 - Northam Airport Upgrades That Council:

1. ACCEPTS the response to the Request for Tender 10 of 2025 – Northam Airport Upgrades from Sterra T/AS Avon Valley Plant & Equipment for $661,900.00 (excl GST).

2. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to make variations to a maximum increase of 10% of the contract value for Request for tender 10 of 2025 – Northam Airport Upgrades from Sterra T/AS Avon Valley Plant & Equipment.

3. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to enter into a contract for Request for Tender 10 of 2025 – Northam Airport Upgrades with Sterra T/AS Avon Valley Plant & Equipment at the discretion of the Shire of Northam in accordance with the specifications contained within the Request for Tender documents.
C.5476 13.3.1 Development Application P25110 - 371/393 Smith Road, Clackline - Retrospective Setback Variation for Water Tanks That Council APPROVES the development application (ref: P25110) for the retrospective application of setback variation for water tanks, located at 371 & 393 Smith Road, Clackline, subject to the following conditions:

1. The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the stamped approved plans.

2. The approval is valid from the date of the local government's decision and does not retrospectively authorise any other unapproved use or development on the premises.

3. The stormwater shall be managed on-site in a manner so that there is no discharge onto the adjoining properties to the satisfaction of the local government.
C.5477 13.4.1 Accounts & Statement of Accounts - December 2025 That Council RECEIVES the payments for the period 1 December to 31 December 2025, as listed below:

•                   Municipal Fund payment cheque numbers 79 to 84 = $90,783.61

•                   Municipal Fund EFT56246 to EFT56508 = $1,715,043.50

•                   Direct Debits = $339,623.33

•                   Superannuation = $167,727.50

•                   Payroll = $904,682.97

TOTAL: $3,217,860.91

that have been made in accordance with the delegated authority reference number (M/F/F/Regs LGA 1995 S5.42).
C.5478 14 Motion to move behind closed doors That Council, in accordance with section 11.1(i) of the Shire of Northam Standing Orders Local Law 2018 and Section 5.23 (2) (a) and (b) of the Local Government Act 1995, meet behind closed doors to consider agenda items:

•  14.1 - Minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Review Committee held on 17 December 2025 as the matters relates to an employee;

•  14.2 - Application under CP.29 Rates Hardship as the matter relates to the personal affairs of a person; and

•  14.3 - Purchase of A14486 as the matter relates to the personal affairs of a person.
C.5479 14.1 Minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Review Committee held on 17 December 2025 That Council RECEIVES the minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Review Committee meeting held on 17 December 2025.
C.5480 14.1 Minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Review Committee held on 17 December 2026 That Council ACCEPTS the Chief Executive Officer Key Performance Indicator Progress Report from 1 October to 12 December 2025, as presented in Attachment 6.1.1 of the Committee minutes.
C.5481 14.2 Application under CP.29 Rates Hardship That Council:

1. APPROVES the payment arrangement of $100.00 per fortnight for the current owner of A12488 until 30 June 2026.

2. APPROVES the payment arrangement of $100.00 per fortnight for the current owner of A78 until 30 June 2026.

3. APPROVES the payment arrangement of $400.00 per month for the current owner of A11761 until 30 June 2026.
C.5482 14.3 Purchase of A14486 That Council BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY REVOKES the previous resolution item 4 in Minute No: C.5131:

“Following acquisition of the property, AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to negotiate the sale of A14486 from the Shire of Northam with adjoining landowner/s.”
C.5483 14.3 Purchase of A14487 That Council:

1. APPROVES the disposal of A14486 by public tender in accordance with section 3.58 of the Local Government Act 1995, with the total sale price being no less than $20,000 excluding GST.

2. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to undertake all actions necessary to advertise, assess, and report the outcomes of the public tender process.
C.5484 14.9.1 Motion to move from behind closed doors That Council move out from behind closed doors.

Special Council Meeting - 7 October 2026

Wednesday, October 7, 2026 - 05:00 PM

Location: Council Chambers, 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam

A Special Meeting of Council has been convened by the Shire President which will take place in the Shire of Northam Council Chambers, 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam:

Date:                   7 October 2026

Time:                   5:00 pm

Purpose:             To consider the following agenda item:

  • 10.1 – Temporary Chief Executive Officer

This meeting is open to the public; however a portion of the meeting will be closed as the business to be considered relates to the recruitment of the Temporary Chief Executive Officer, in accordance with section 5.23(2)(b) of the Local Government Act 1995.

Please be advised that this meeting will be livestreamed and audio-recorded and made available on the Shire of Northam’s YouTube channel.

DEBBIE TERELINCK
CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICE

Special Council Meeting - 3 September 2026

Thursday, September 3, 2026 - 05:00 PM

Location: Council Chambers, 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam

A Special Council Meeting was held in the Council Chambers, located at 395 Fitzgerald Street, Northam on 3 September 2026 at 5:00 pm.

Summary of Decisions:

    Motion No. Item No Subject Motion
    C.5626 9.1 Minutes from the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee Meeting held on 18 August 2026 That Council RECEIVES the minutes from the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee meeting held on 18 August 2026
    C.5627 9.1 Minutes from the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee Meeting held on 18 August 2027 That Council:
    1. ADOPTS the Compliance Audit Return for the period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 as presented in Attachment 7.7.1.
    2. AUTHORISES the Chief Executive Officer to submit the certified Compliance Audit Return and supporting documentation to the Local Government Inspectorate in accordance with the prescribed requirements.
    3. RECEIVES the May 2026 to July 2026 update on the internal compliance checks as provided in Attachments 7.2.1; and
    4. ACCEPTS the risk in relation to the timeframe for making Building Services Levy Payments and REQUESTS the Chief Executive Officer to no longer report these internal compliance check findings.
    5. RECEIVES the August 2026 update as provided in Attachment 7.3.1 in relation to the progress made towards the Privacy and Responsible Information Sharing (PRIS) Action Plan.
    6. RECEIVES the update as provided in Attachment 7.4.1 in relation to the progress made towards implementation of the ICT Strategy Plan.
    7. NOTES the measures outlined in the report to manage the ERP project delivery risks including additional project phasing, extended delivery timeframes and engagement of external resourcing to assist with implementation.
    8. RECEIVES the Internal Reviews and Audit Actions update as presented in Attachments 7.5.1, 7.5.2 and 7.5.3.
    9. RECEIVES the August 2026 update on the Shire of Northam Strategic Risk Register, including the status of overdue and non-compliant Strategic Risk Management Treatments.
    C.5628 10 MATTERS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS That Council, in accordance with section 11.1(i) of the Shire of Northam Standing Orders Local Law 2018 and Section 5.23 (2) (b) of the Local Government Act 1995, meet behind closed doors to consider agenda item 10.1 - Minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Selection Panel Meeting held on 28 August 2026 as the matter relates to the recruitment of the Chief Executive Officer.
    C.5629 10.1 MINUTES FROM THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER SELECTION PANEL MEETING HELD ON 28 AUGUST 2026 That Council RECEIVES the minutes from the Chief Executive Officer Selection Panel meeting held on 28 August 2026.
    C.5630 10.1 MINUTES FROM THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER SELECTION PANEL MEETING HELD ON 28 AUGUST 2027 That Council:
    1. ADOPTS, by absolute majority, the Chief Executive Officer Job Description Form and Position Selection Criteria as provided in Attachment 6.1.3, for the purposes of the Chief Executive Officer recruitment process.
    2. AUTHORISES advertisement of the Chief Executive Officer position in accordance with the Local Government Act 1995, the Local Government (Administration) Regulations 1996 and the Shire of Northam Standards for CEO Recruitment, Performance and Termination.
    C.5631 10 MATTERS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS That Council move out from behind closed doors.
